# Check Engine SEO

> Check Engine SEO is a Mac and Windows app that audits any website on your own computer: 99
> checks across 13 areas, then one ranked plan of what to fix, in order, with the
> markup to paste and a client-ready PDF report. It costs $59, paid once; there is no
> subscription.

The crawl and the report stay on your computer, and there is no account. The app sends
three anonymous counts, with no site address or audit result. Five optional checks are
on by default and reach outside it: Google PageSpeed Insights is sent the addresses of
the homepage and top pages; Google's public autocomplete is sent the site's topic
words, typed by the user or read off its titles, headings and descriptions; DNS is
asked about the mail domains the site publishes; the audited server is asked what it
tells AI crawlers; and https://docketseo.app/data/knowledge.json serves a knowledge
file. Offline mode turns all five off. Checking links to other sites, and rendering a
few pages as a browser would, also reach the sites and services those pages link to or
load. The licence key is checked with the payment provider when it is activated and
about once a day after that. The app asks https://docketseo.app/updater.json whether
an update exists. While its activation screen is showing on a copy with no key, it
asks https://docketseo.app/offer.json for the current price and offer and whether the
founding offer is still open.

Check Engine is written by Matt Kerr and sold by Kerr & Company LLC, of Grand Rapids,
Michigan, United States.

## What it checks

- 99 checks across 13 areas: AI search visibility, Brand consistency, Content quality,
  Conversion & landing pages, Crawlability & indexing, Links, Local business SEO,
  Tracking & campaign readiness, On-page SEO, Speed & Core Web Vitals, Structured
  data, Security & trust and Social & sharing.
- Every finding is ranked by impact against the effort of fixing it, and carries its
  evidence: the page it is on, the exact value found there, and the fix.
- AI search visibility: each AI crawler is checked separately (OAI-SearchBot for
  ChatGPT Search, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot) and kept apart from training
  crawlers such as GPTBot. Google-Extended is reported as what it is: Gemini training
  and Gemini Apps grounding, with no effect on AI Overviews. Check Engine checks robots.txt
  rules for 22 AI crawlers. A separate check requests your homepage as 9 AI crawlers
  plus Googlebot to find server refusals the file cannot show.
- A command-line interface ships inside the app. `checkengine audit` exits non-zero on a
  critical issue, so CI can fail a build before it ships.
- [All 99 checks, by area](https://checkengineseo.com/learn/what-docket-checks/): the complete list, generated from the shipped build so it cannot drift from the product
- [How Check Engine decides what to fix first](https://checkengineseo.com/learn/priority-model/): severity, impact, reach and effort, and the formula that combines them

## Sample report

- [Sample report (PDF)](https://docketseo.app/assets/docket-sample-report.pdf): a full sample of the client-ready PDF Check Engine writes: score, scorecard, ranked plan, paste-ready markup, and a page on what was and was not measured

## Requirements

- A Mac with Apple silicon or Intel running macOS 12 or later.
- The Mac app is a 31.4 MB download, signed with a Developer ID and notarised by
  Apple.
- Or a PC with 64-bit Windows: the installer is an 18.1 MB download, signed by Kerr &
  Company LLC.
- A command-line build for Linux x86_64 is on the download page.
- AI assistants can run it: Check Engine speaks MCP over stdio, so Claude Code (claude mcp
  add docket -- /Applications/Docket.app/Contents/Resources/docket/docket mcp), Claude
  Desktop and the ChatGPT desktop app can audit a site with it. Setup:
  https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/audit-your-site-from-an-ai-assistant/

## Price and licence

- $59, paid once, in US dollars. Not a subscription: there is no renewal date and
  nothing to cancel.
- Launch price: $29.50 once, through 30 November. From 1 December: $59. The Buy link
  applies the code FOUNDINGDOCKET at checkout (if the checkout shows $59, enter it
  under "Have a discount code?").
- From 1 December, at $59, four payments of $14.75 with Klarna or Afterpay, two weeks
  apart. The Launch price of $29.50 is paid in one payment: the checkout offers no
  instalments under $50.01.
- Free: your score, how many problems in each category, and the top problem in full
  with its fix. Pro: the rest of the problems, the ranked fix plan and the markup to
  paste. The free version needs no key and no account, and runs the same full audit;
  buying unlocks the audit already run, with no second crawl.
- The licence key arrives by email with the receipt and is pasted into the app once.
  One licence covers up to 3 computers at a time, Mac or Windows: activating Check Engine on
  a computer uses one, and deactivating one moves the licence to another.
- The licence belongs to the person or company that paid. It covers any number of
  websites, including clients' sites, and the work can be billed to those clients. The
  application itself may not be resold, sublicensed or redistributed.

## Refunds

- Thirty days from the date of purchase, no conditions and no questions asked. The
  full purchase price goes back to the payment method it came from.
- To ask, write to support@docketseo.app or reply to the receipt Dodo Payments sends.
- A refund revokes the licence key, and within about a day the copy goes back to the
  free version.

## What it does not do

- No per-page backlinks or anchor text, and no monthly search volumes.
- Copy-quality checks are English-only; the technical checks work in any language.
- Not built, on purpose: rank tracking, a cloud version, team accounts, server-side
  scheduling and uptime monitoring.
- Reports can carry your own name and logo in place of Check Engine's (paid version:
  Reports, then Report branding; or checkengine audit --brand-name and --brand-logo).
- Scheduled re-audits run only while Check Engine is open: the schedule is a thread inside
  the app, so quitting it stops the clock.

## Frequently asked questions

- Is Check Engine free? Free: your score, how many problems in each category, and the top
  problem in full with its fix. Pro: the rest of the problems, the ranked fix plan and
  the markup to paste. Launch price: $29.50 once, through 30 November. From 1
  December: $59. There is a 30-day refund. There is no subscription and nothing to
  cancel.
- What if it isn't for me? Ask for a refund within 30 days of buying and you get your
  money back. No conditions and no questions. Write to support@docketseo.app, or reply
  to the receipt the payment processor emails you. The licence key is revoked, so the
  copy goes back to the free version.
- How many computers does one licence cover? Up to 3 computers at a time, Mac or
  Windows. Activating Check Engine on a computer uses one; deactivate it to move the licence
  to another. On a Mac: Apple silicon or Intel, macOS 12 or later.
- Are updates included? Yes. While Check Engine is on version 1.x, every update is free and
  installs through the app's own updater. Whether a future 2.0 is a paid upgrade has
  not been decided; if it ever is, the copy you paid for keeps working.
- Can I use it for client work? Yes. Audit any number of sites (yours, a client's, a
  prospect's or a competitor's) and charge clients for the work. The licence belongs
  to the person or company that paid; it may not be resold or sublicensed.
- Does it run on Windows? Yes. Check Engine v1.3.161 has an installer for 64-bit Windows,
  18.1 MB, signed by Kerr & Company LLC. It is on the download page beside the Mac app
  and a command-line build for Linux x86_64.
- How do I get help? Email support@docketseo.app. Questions whose answers would help
  the next person can go on the public issue tracker instead.
- Does Check Engine send my site data anywhere? The crawl and the report stay on your
  computer, and there is no account. The app sends three anonymous counts, with no
  site address or audit result. Five optional checks, on by default, reach outside it:
  Core Web Vitals from Google PageSpeed, which is sent the addresses of your homepage
  and top pages; a deliverability test on the addresses your site publishes, which
  looks up their mail domains in DNS; what your server tells AI crawlers; a knowledge
  refresh; and Google's public autocomplete for topic suggestions, which is sent your
  site's topic words. The knowledge refresh fetches docketseo.app/data/knowledge.json.
  Offline mode turns all five off, and every report names the ones that ran. Checking
  your links to other sites, and rendering a few pages as a browser would, also reach
  the sites and services those pages link to or load. The licence key is checked with
  our payment provider when you activate it and about once a day after that.
- How is Check Engine different from Screaming Frog? Screaming Frog gives you raw crawl data
  and leaves the interpretation to you. Check Engine ranks every finding by impact against
  effort and gives you an ordered plan with the exact markup to paste. Screaming Frog
  supports custom XPath extraction, which Check Engine does not. Both run JavaScript: Check Engine
  renders a sample of every audit automatically, in the WebKit engine macOS already
  ships.
- Can Check Engine tell me if ChatGPT can see my website? Yes. Check Engine checks each AI crawler
  separately (OAI-SearchBot for ChatGPT Search, PerplexityBot and Claude-SearchBot)
  and distinguishes them from training crawlers like GPTBot, which many sites block
  deliberately. It also says what Google-Extended does: it governs Gemini training and
  Gemini Apps, not AI Overviews, which follow Googlebot.

- [Free JSON-LD checker](https://checkengineseo.com/tools/json-ld-checker/): invalid JSON by line and column, and the properties each structured data item needs for a rich result

## Fix guides people search for most

- [How to fix CLS issues (cumulative layout shift)](https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/fix-layout-shift/): Layout shift is almost always images with no width and height. The fix, the four other causes, and why a crawler can report the risk but not the score.
- [How to fix hreflang tags with errors (return tags)](https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/fix-hreflang-return-tags/): hreflang only works when the link goes both ways. Why one-way declarations are ignored, the four ways a set breaks, and why canonical must agree.
- [How to fix duplicate title tags, and what it won't fix](https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/fix-duplicate-title-tags/): Duplicate titles are not a penalty. They let the wrong page on your site win the query and waste the one line of the result you get to write.
- [How to write title tags that fit (width, not characters)](https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/write-title-tags-that-fit/): Search engines truncate by pixel width, not character count, which makes the usual advice wrong on any site that is not entirely English.
- [How to run a JavaScript SEO audit (step by step)](https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/javascript-seo-audit/): A JavaScript SEO audit compares the HTML your server sends against the rendered page, in five steps. Which of the three gaps you have decides the fix.
- [How to fix conflicting canonical tags](https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/fix-conflicting-canonicals/): Two canonicals on one page, canonicals pointing at noindex pages or another domain, and the section-wide mistake that can cost a site its long tail.
- [Content audit with Ahrefs: which tool does what](https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/content-audit/): Ahrefs sells no product called Content Audit. What the job is, which of their tools covers which part, and the order that wastes least time.
- [hreflang and html lang mismatch: which one you have](https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/fix-lang-attribute-mismatch/): Three different faults share that description and have three different fixes. How to tell them apart in a minute, and which one to fix first.
- [Backlink audit: which questions are worth paying for](https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/backlink-audit/): Ahrefs sells no product called Backlink Audit. The three questions an audit asks, which tool answers each, and what an open link graph cannot.
- [How to redirect http:// to https://, and when it won't](https://checkengineseo.com/how-to/redirect-http-to-https/): A 301 from http:// to https://, host by host. Plus the certificate state that blocks the Enforce HTTPS setting, and the DNS record that causes it.
